what_it_does: Data centers save money by running two kinds of work on the same server at once: latency-critical jobs (like responding to a search query in milliseconds) and best-effort background jobs (like batch processing). The problem is that they share the same memory bus, and the background job can hog memory bandwidth and slow the critical job below acceptable response-time limits. Pivot fixes this by giving priority to memory requests from the critical job at every level — the fast on-chip cache hierarchy and the main memory controller — but only for loads that are actually stalling the processor's out-of-order execution pipeline (the part that tries to overlap multiple instructions). An offline profiling step identifies exactly which memory reads are on the critical path, so the priority mechanism fires precisely rather than flooding every critical-job request with elevated priority.
